circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island designed by Hermann Tilke, has been the home of Formula One's season finale since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern venue to join the F1 calendar, following Bahrain and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street layout encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne that hosts the Australian Grand Prix each year, alongside various support categories including the Supercars Championship round. Holding an FIA Grade 1 classification, the venue serves as a premier motorsport destination for multiple racing series.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit originally operated as Österreichring, serving as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following substantial modifications and a rebranding, the track resumed hosting the prestigious race from 1997 onwards under its new identity.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital that stretches 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit first hosted a grand prix in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before becoming a permanent fixture on the calendar as the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km facility that hosted the first-ever Formula One Grand Prix in the Middle East that same year and continues to stage the annual Bahrain Grand Prix alongside other racing series. The venue, which holds a FIA Grade 1 license and features multiple track configurations, has also accommodated drag racing, endurance competitions, and briefly hosted V8 Supercar events between 2006 and 2010.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located near Barcelona in Montmeló, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometres and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for teams across different disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: This Belgian circuit, stretching over 7 kilometers through the Ardennes region, has been hosting motorsport events since 1925 and featured in Formula One's inaugural 1950 season. The venue has maintained its status as the home of the Belgian Grand Prix with remarkable consistency, appearing on the calendar annually from 1985 onward, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, this 4. 361-kilometre motor racing circuit serves as the home of the FIA Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond its primary role in Formula One, the venue has hosted numerous other major racing series including sports car championships, open-wheel competitions, and various NASCAR categories throughout its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Shanghai International Circuit, located in Jiading, is China's premier racing venue and home to the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before returning in 2024. The track also accommodates electric motorsport racing, having added an ePrix event to its calendar from 2024 onwards.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone Circuit is located in England near the Northamptonshire villages of Silverstone and Whittlebury, serving as the traditional home of the British Grand Prix since 1948. The venue gained historic significance when it hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950, and after rotating with other British circuits during the 1955-1986 period, it became the permanent host from 1987 onwards. In addition to Formula One, the track also stages the British MotoGP round.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Mogyoród, is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held in the Eastern Bloc when it debuted in 1986. Built in just eight months, faster than any other Formula One venue at the time, the track was constructed outside the city near a major highway after plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park were abandoned.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Monza Circuit is a 5. 793 km speedway constructed in 1922 and ranks among Europe's oldest purpose-built racing facilities. The venue hosts the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949 (except during a 1980 closure for renovation), making it one of only four circuits to feature continuously on the Formula One calendar from the championship's inception, and it earns the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its characteristic long straights and rapid corner configurations.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, operated by Honda, is a 5. 807-kilometre Japanese motorsport venue situated in Mie Prefecture with a 155,000-person capacity. The track is primarily recognized as a Formula One Grand Prix host and Japanese Super Formula racing destination.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through the heart of Paradise, Nevada's famous entertainment district along Las Vegas Boulevard. The layout weaves past iconic venues and hotels such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, making it one of the most visually distinctive tracks on the Formula One calendar.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both prominent racing drivers who died in separate accidents during the 1960s and early 1970s. The track returned to hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix in 2015 after a 23-year absence, though the race had been held there previously on an alternate configuration ending in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners designed by Apex Circuit Design for the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One calendar in 2022. The track achieves qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph and has since accommodated Formula E racing on an adapted configuration starting in the 2025–26 season.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street layout that winds through the urban streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, encircling the harbour area of Monaco. The track is frequently known as "Monte Carlo," reflecting that the majority of its course traverses the Monte Carlo district of the principality.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the revived Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 until 2026. The circuit earned its "Roller coaster in the Dunes" nickname from its dramatic elevation changes and heavily banked corners like Tarzan and Hugenholtz, which wind through the North Sea dunes and create a uniquely demanding racing experience.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Lusail International Circuit, situated north of Doha in Qatar, spans 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight and holds FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km motorsport facility in São Paulo, Brazil, originally opened in 1940 and renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace. The counterclockwise circuit also features a karting track dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural running in 2021.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's waterfront district, incorporating sections of both the Downtown Core and Kallang planning areas into its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya in Montmeló near Barcelona offers a 4. 657 km layout featuring extended straights combined with diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for all-round racing performance. Holding an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodating 140,700 spectators, the track serves as a premier venue for international motorsport competitions.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas, situated in Austin, Texas, is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 FIA-certified racing facility that serves as the primary venue for the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the track hosts multiple international motorsport competitions including MotoGP and World Endurance Championship events, along with various North American racing series.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver currently competing for Williams in Formula One, representing Thailand in the championship.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: The Spanish driver currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, having previously captured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006, along with 32 Grand Prix victories across his lengthy career. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, winning the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship and two Le Mans 24-hour races, making him the sole competitor to claim both F1 and sportscar world titles.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli secured the 2026 Formula One World Drivers' Championship with Mercedes, setting a record as the sport's youngest champion, having claimed nine race victories since entering the series in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One as a member of the Audi team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas brings experience from 13 seasons of Formula One racing to his current role with Cadillac. Having secured two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during his time with Mercedes, Bottas has accumulated 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One for Alpine.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, serves as a reserve for Haas in Formula One while competing in sports car racing with AF Corse in the Asian Le Mans Series. He made seven Grand Prix appearances between 2024 and 2025, having previously raced in the European Le Mans Series.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: A French-Algerian racing driver competing for Red Bull Racing, Isack Alexandre Hadjar represents France in Formula One competition.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has secured seven world championship titles, equalling Michael Schumacher's record. He holds numerous career records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi, having established himself as a competitive force in motorsport. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he achieved significant success in endurance racing by winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor currently driving for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver competing for Ferrari, finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship and has claimed nine race victories during his nine seasons in Formula One.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen has competed intermittently in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and again from 2022-2024, before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship, representing BMW as a factory driver for the WRT team.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British Formula One driver who secured the 2025 drivers' championship while racing for McLaren. Across his eight seasons in the sport, he has claimed 14 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French driver who recently drove for Haas in Formula One. Earlier in his career, he achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while racing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez, a Mexican driver competing for Cadillac in Formula One, finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while with Red Bull. Throughout his 15-season career in the sport, he has claimed six Grand Prix victories.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having claimed nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four-year career in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career. Known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," Ricciardo has since retired from the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, having secured four Grand Prix victories over his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant competed in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to endurance racing. He is now set to drive for Ford in the FIA World Endurance Championship, having previously raced in the LMGT3 category with Proton Competition in the same series.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver currently competing in Formula One for Aston Martin, where he continues his career in motorsport's premier racing series.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, competed as a full-time Formula One competitor between 2021 and 2025 before transitioning to a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: A Dutch and Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing, Verstappen has claimed four consecutive Formula One World Drivers' Championships between 2021 and 2024. Over his 12-season career, he has accumulated 74 Grand Prix victories while racing under the Dutch flag.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor to date, raced in the championship from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. He currently holds the position of reserve driver for the team.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed under the Alpine banner since 2021 as Renault's factory operation, following a rebranding from its previous Renault F1 Team identity to highlight the Alpine sports car marque. Operating under Groupe Renault's ownership throughout this period, the team maintained its works status until the French manufacturer's withdrawal from the championship at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has maintained involvement in Formula One across multiple team structures, with the current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team designation.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team, having participated in every World Championship season since the sport's inception in 1950. Known colloquially as "the Prancing Horse" after their iconic emblem, the team has maintained continuous involvement in the championship longer than any other competitor.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American Formula One team in 2014, debuting in the 2016 season as a newcomer to the sport. Leadership changed in early 2024 when Ayao Komatsu took over as team principal from Guenther Steiner, who had led the outfit since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, this Swiss engineering and racing outfit initially competed in endurance racing before joining Formula One in 1993, where it operated as an independent constructor through numerous iterations. The team achieved notable success including overall victory at Le Mans in 1989 before departing the grid in 2025 as the fourth-longest-serving constructor by race count, with its operations subsequently acquired by Audi AG to serve as the foundation for Audi's own factory effort.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under the McLaren Mastercard banner. The team operates as part of the McLaren Group, which is fully owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 through both team ownership and engine supply. The current iteration, Mercedes-AMG Petronas, operates from Brackley under a German licence, with ownership shared equally among Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff as of January 2022. The marque's racing efforts are traditionally associated with the "Silver Arrows" nickname.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull's two-team operation. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the squad operates as Red Bull's sister team alongside the main Red Bull Racing outfit.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that debuted in 2024 as the second team owned by Red Bull GmbH alongside Red Bull Racing. Operating from facilities in Faenza and Milton Keynes, the squad represents Red Bull's expanded presence on the grid with a dual-team structure.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, operating under an Austrian licence despite being based in England, emerged as a Formula One competitor in 2005 under the stewardship of Christian Horner, who led the team until his departure in early 2025. As one of two racing operations controlled by Red Bull GmbH, the team represents the multinational corporation's primary Formula One entry, with Laurent Mekies assuming leadership following Horner's exit.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, the British Formula One constructor founded by Frank Williams and Patrick Head in 1977, evolved from Frank Williams's earlier unsuccessful racing operation. Based at their Grove, Oxfordshire facility, the team competes in the 2026 season as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and maintains an established presence as both a team and constructor in the sport.
